newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska fed cattle trade very slow - private.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska fed cattle trade very slow - private.

text.p: Nebraska feedlot cattle markets near midday on Tuesday were slow, with only a handful of cattle reportedly sold.

Market sources said about 400 steers likely to grade select and choice sold at $65.00 per cwt on a live basis, delivered, and at $102.00 per cwt on a dressed basis. The sales were too light for an adequate market test, they said.
Other bids dressed basis bids were mostly at $102.00 but passed by some owners asking $104.00 to $105.00.
Hot, humid weather moved into Nebraska this weekend and was expected to remain through the week.

The weather could impact weight gains, especially in the eastern part of the state if evening temperatures and humidity do not come down, sources said. However, for the most part the weather has not had a significant impact on cattle performance, one Nebraska source said.
